title: College Readiness (Follow-Up)
plain_title: Checkup on how city schools prepare students for college
what_they_audited: How far New York City Public Schools has gone in carrying out the four recommendations from a 2022 state audit of how well the school system prepares students for college.
background: New York City Public Schools, the nation's largest school system, served about 900,000 students in the 2023-24 school year. The initial audit found that in a cohort of 71,210 students expected to graduate by August 2019, as many as 23% did not graduate on time, 38% did not persist in college for 6 months after enrolling and 45% of a 291-student sample were not college ready.

findings.plain: The school system has made significant progress since the initial audit. All four of the original recommendations have been implemented.
findings.quote: Of the initial report’s four audit recommendations, all four have been implemented.

findings.plain: Graduation rates still outpace college readiness. In 2024, 83% of high school students citywide graduated while only 52% were considered college ready, and the system has since added a grade point average component and a career component to its readiness metric.
findings.quote: In 2024, 83% of high school students citywide graduated, while only 52% were considered college ready.

numbers.label: High school students citywide who graduated in 2024

recommendations: The report makes no formal recommendations.
implementation_note: Of the four recommendations in the 2022 audit, the follow-up found all four implemented.
